newsitem.title: USA: Telesoft may have Q2 charge.
newsitem.headline: Telesoft may have Q2 charge.

text.p: Telesoft Corp said Thursday it had restructured the ownership of its GoodNet subsidiary, a National Internet Service Provider offering data communication over the Internet, and may take a related charge in the second quarter.
The treatment of the transaction from an accounting standpoint is not yet resolved, but the deal's $393,000 cash payment could result in a pre-tax charge to earnings for the second quarter, it said.
Under the new ownership structure, Telesoft said it will own 75 percent of GoodNet Corp's common stock, and David Jemmett, who will continue as president of GoodNet, will own the rest.

Telesoft said Jemmett, David Brady and certain minority shareholders (the former GoodNet LLC principals who sold the company to Telesoft for a combination of cash and stock in April 1996) had agreed to relinquish claims to up to 280,833 shares of Telesoft.

Brady has resigned from GoodNet and relinquished his claim to Telesoft common stock in exchange for $393,000 cash plus payments of $10,000 per month for five years, which will be paid by GoodNet, it said.
As part of the agreement, Telesoft said, $4.0 million of capital infused by Telesoft into GoodNet over the past 12 months will be reclassified as debt payable to Telesoft.
Telesoft said it will continue to make capital available to GoodNet for equipment purchases and strategic acquisitions.
